title: Brush Up: The 5-Minute Daily News - AI/Tech, Biz, World
description: Your definitive morning intelligence download. Every day shortly after 7:00 AM EST, we bypass the noise to deliver the critical shifts in AI, Global Business, and Macroeconomics that define the modern landscape. Brush up on the news while you brush up your smile.
latestSummary:
Waabi secured a $1 billion investment from Uber, planning to deploy 25,000 robotaxis on the Uber platform, signaling a major expansion in autonomous vehicle services. Anthropic raised $20 billion, reflecting investor confidence in AI, while OpenAI launched Prism for AI-integrated research. Google expanded its AI Plus plan globally and utilized Gemini for Indian college entrance exams.

In business, Pinterest’s 15% workforce reduction highlighted AI-driven reorganization, and the semiconductor industry saw strong demand, boosting Texas Instruments and ASML’s stock performance. Lockheed Martin and other major defense contractors secured significant contracts, and AT&T exceeded profit forecasts. Revolut began offering full banking services in Mexico.

Globally, the conflict in Ukraine escalated with a deadly drone strike. Former South Korean First Lady received a 20-month prison sentence for bribery, and Rwanda sought £100 million from the UK regarding the asylum deal. Former Iraqi Prime Minister Maliki denounced threats from Donald Trump, and President Trump indicated a de-escalation of government actions in Minnesota following the Alex Pretti shooting.

title: Overnight Market Brief - Bridging the Global Gap. Daily.
description:
While North America sleeps, the global economy keeps moving. Overnight Market Brief is your essential pre-market digest, designed for traders, serious investors, and professionals who need to hit the ground running.
Most North American investors miss 50% of the market story because it happens in Tokyo, Hong Kong, and London. We bridge that gap. Every morning at 8:00 AM ET, we deliver a concise, data-driven breakdown and full global picture in under 10 minutes, just in time for your morning commute.
latestSummary:
Wall Street opened firmly in risk-on mode on January 28, 2026, driven by a weakening US Dollar and anticipation of the Federal Reserve’s upcoming decision. The S&P 500 rose 0.41% and the Nasdaq 100 climbed 0.89%, fueled by a broad equity rally. The 10-Year Treasury Yield remained steady at 4.244%, while the US Dollar Index decreased by 0.06%. Notably, gold experienced a significant surge, up 3.74%, reflecting safe-haven demand or inflation concerns.

Overnight, Asian markets showed mixed performance with Hong Kong’s Hang Seng surging 2.57% and Greater China’s Composite advancing 0.27%. European markets were cautious, influenced by Germany’s downgraded growth forecast and declining Irish retail sales. US futures were higher, with S&P 500 futures up 0.25% and Nasdaq 100 futures up 0.83%, reflecting a rotation into tech and growth stocks.

Key catalysts for the upcoming session include continued anticipation of the Federal Reserve decision, Australian CPI data impacting RBA rate hike expectations, and the German government’s revised growth forecast. The market’s path of least resistance appears to be higher, contingent on data releases.

title: Post-market Recap
description:
Did the market "rally into the close" or "fade the open"? The Post-Market Recap goes beyond the green and red arrows to analyze the structure of the trading day. This daily briefing dissects the inter-market correlations that drove the session.
Every afternoon, we cover:
Macro Causality: Connecting the dots between the 10-Year Yield, the Dollar Index, and Equities.
Tech & AI Pulse: A dedicated segment on the semiconductor ecosystem and Big Tech performance.
Market Breadth: Analyzing Volatility (VIX) and Sector Rotation to gauge genuine institutional sentiment.
Closing Catalysts: Identifying the specific news and data that triggered late-day reversals.
latestSummary:
Here’s a summary of the AGI Era Post-Market Recap, approximately 150 words:

Today’s market action presented a mixed picture, with the S&P 500 and Nasdaq 100 rising while the Dow Jones Industrial Average declined. The S&P 500 gained 0.41% to 6978.6, and the Nasdaq jumped 0.88% to 25939.744, driven by tech sector strength, particularly the XLK and XLU funds. The Dow fell 409 points, reflecting headwinds in traditional industries. Trading volume was lighter than average, suggesting a lack of strong institutional buying.

The weaker US Dollar Index (down 1.28%) fueled gains in crude oil (up 3.00%), benefiting multinational corporations and potentially contributing to inflationary pressures. Artificial intelligence stocks led the way, with Nvidia, Microsoft, and Apple all posting gains. Texas Instruments saw a significant after-hours surge.

Despite a concerning drop in consumer confidence, the housing market showed resilience. Investors will be closely watching the Federal Reserve’s response to the dollar’s weakness and the evolving impact of consumer spending data.

title: Geopolitical Updates
description: Beyond the headlines lies strategy. Geopolitical Updates is your daily guide to the evolving global order. Each episode provides a rapid scan of the day's top international stories, followed by a deep-dive analysis of the single most impactful event shifting the geopolitical landscape. From tension in the South China Sea to economic statecraft in Europe, we explain not just what happened today, but why it matters for tomorrow. Delivered daily at 7 PM ET.
latestSummary:
The most significant news today involves the groundbreaking India-EU trade agreement, dubbed the “mother of all trade deals,” marking a strategic realignment amid rising protectionism and U.S. tensions. This pact, securing preferential access for India to the EU’s vast market and vice versa, aims to bolster both economies and reduce reliance on the U.S.

Domestically, Spain is preparing to grant legal status to approximately 500,000 undocumented migrants, a move intended to address labor shortages and formalize the informal economy, though critics express concerns about potential increased migration pressures.

Internationally, the U.S. has deployed ICE agents to the Winter Olympics in Italy, sparking condemnation and diplomatic tensions. Simultaneously, President Trump has imposed new tariffs on South Korean goods, escalating trade disputes and potentially disrupting supply chains. Canadian Prime Minister Carney vehemently denied walking back his Davos statements following a Trump phone call, highlighting ongoing trade tensions. Finally, Rwanda is pursuing legal action against the UK over the failed migrant deal.

These developments collectively paint a picture of a shifting global landscape, with India and the EU positioning themselves as alternative economic powers and navigating a complex, increasingly fragmented international trade environment.
